questions.questionText: Which of the following numbers is prime?
questions.explanation: 87 = 3 × 29, 91 = 7 × 13 and 93 = 3 × 31 are composite. 97 has no prime divisor up to 9 (2, 3, 5, 7), so it is prime.
questions.shortcut: Test divisibility by primes up to √n.

questions.questionText: What is the smallest prime number greater than 90?
questions.shortcut: Skip evens and multiples of 3, 5, 7.

questions.questionText: What is the sum of the first eight prime numbers?
questions.shortcut: List the primes and add carefully.

questions.questionText: How many prime numbers are there from 1 to 50?
questions.shortcut: Remember the count: 25 primes below 100, 15 below 50.

questions.questionText: What is the largest prime factor of 2310?
questions.shortcut: Divide out small primes first.

questions.questionText: Which is the only even prime number?
questions.explanation: Every even number greater than 2 is divisible by 2 and hence composite. So 2 is the only even prime.
questions.shortcut: Memorise it.

questions.questionText: What is the smallest prime number that is also a factor of 3003?
questions.explanation: 3003 is odd, so 2 is not a factor. Digit sum = 6, so 3 divides it: 3003 = 3 × 1001. The smallest prime factor is 3.
questions.shortcut: Test 2, 3, 5 in order.

questions.questionText: To test whether 391 is prime by trial division, what is the largest prime you need to try as a divisor?
questions.explanation: √391 ≈ 19.8, so test primes up to 19. In fact 391 = 17 × 23 is composite, and 17 is found while testing.
questions.shortcut: Test all primes ≤ √n.

questions.questionText: Two prime numbers have sum 60 and product 899. What is the larger prime?
questions.shortcut: Use (q − p)² = (p + q)² − 4pq.

questions.questionText: What is the largest prime factor of 8051?
questions.explanation: 8051 = 8100 − 49 = 90² − 7² = (90 − 7)(90 + 7) = 83 × 97. Both are prime, so the largest is 97.
questions.shortcut: Look for a difference of squares.

questions.questionText: What is the sum of the distinct prime factors of 3003?
questions.shortcut: Factorise using 1001 = 7 × 11 × 13.

questions.questionText: The expression n² + n + 41 gives primes for many natural numbers n. What is the smallest natural number n for which it is composite?
questions.explanation: It stays prime for n = 1 to 39, and fails at n = 40: 40² + 40 + 41 = 1681 = 41².
questions.shortcut: Look for n where n² + n + 41 is a multiple of 41, i.e. n = 40.

questions.questionText: How many prime numbers lie between 100 and 130?
questions.shortcut: Check only numbers of the form 6k ± 1.

questions.questionText: Every prime greater than 3 is of the form 6k ± 1. How many primes below 60 are of the form 6k + 1?
questions.explanation: Primes below 60 that leave remainder 1 on division by 6: 7, 13, 19, 31, 37, 43. Count = 6.

questions.questionText: If p is a prime greater than 3, then p² − 1 is always divisible by which of the following?
questions.explanation: p is of the form 6k ± 1, so p² − 1 = (p − 1)(p + 1) is a product of two consecutive even numbers (one a multiple of 4) and also contains a multiple of 3. So 8 × 3 = 24 always divides it.
questions.shortcut: (p − 1)(p + 1): even, multiple of 8 and of 3.

questions.questionText: How many prime numbers p are there such that p, p + 2 and p + 4 are all prime?
questions.explanation: Among p, p + 2, p + 4 one is a multiple of 3 for any p. So all three can be prime only if that multiple is 3 itself: (3, 5, 7). Exactly 1 such prime.
questions.shortcut: Three numbers in steps of 2 cover all residues mod 3.

questions.questionText: The product of two consecutive primes is 1763. What is the larger prime?
questions.explanation: √1763 ≈ 42, so look at the primes near 42: 41 × 43 = 1763. The larger prime is 43.
questions.shortcut: Take the square root and look at adjacent primes.

questions.questionText: How many primes p less than 100 are there such that p + 6 is also prime?
questions.shortcut: Enumerate primes below 100 and test p + 6.

questions.questionText: In how many ways can 50 be written as the sum of two prime numbers (order not counted)?
questions.shortcut: Try each prime ≤ 25 and check the partner.

questions.questionText: Find the sum of all prime numbers p below 30 for which 2p + 1 is also prime.
questions.shortcut: Test 2p + 1 for each prime below 30.

questions.questionText: What is the greatest prime factor of 3¹² − 1?
questions.shortcut: Use a² − b² repeatedly.

questions.questionText: How many two-digit prime numbers have the property that the number obtained by reversing the digits is also prime (palindromic primes such as 11 are included)?
questions.shortcut: Primes with digits 2, 4, 5, 6, 8, 0 in the tens or units place are ruled out.

questions.questionText: What is the sum of all prime numbers between 50 and 70?
questions.shortcut: List 6k ± 1 numbers and test them.

questions.questionText: What is the total number of prime factors (counting repetitions) in the product 4¹¹ × 7⁵ × 11²?
questions.explanation: 4¹¹ = 2²² contributes 22 prime factors, 7⁵ contributes 5 and 11² contributes 2. Total = 22 + 5 + 2 = 29.
questions.shortcut: Convert every base to primes first.
